top_story.headline: Court orders former treasurer to repay $29,413.77 to Forward Together PAC
top_story.dek: The committee told the FEC on Tuesday, in answer to an RFAI, that restitution is owed to it.
paragraphs: Forward Together PAC filed a Form 99 on October 6 answering a September 1 Request for Additional Information on its 2026 July Quarterly Report. The FEC's letter had noted a Schedule D debt described as "Court-ordered restitution payment owed to the Committee" and said it appeared tied to an unauthorized use of committee funds.

The committee says a federal court ordered its former treasurer, Katherine Buchanan, to pay $29,413.77, that it first explained this in a Form 99 on July 20, 2026, and that it is still working with the FEC. It cites FEC advisory opinions 1991-38 and 2005-04 for carrying the amount as a debt owed to it.

sections.headline: Five sitting members' committees get FEC letters or file responses
paragraphs: Two Delegates account for seven RFAIs; the rest are a Senate letter with a 24-page excessive-contribution attachment and two House items.

items: Rep. Mary Miller (R-IL), Mary Miller for Congress — Form 99 answering a September 3 RFAI on the July Quarterly Report. The FEC had asked about three debts to Launchpad Strategies ($9,262.03, $9,130.84 and $9,646.48; $28,039.35 total) that disappeared from the report. The committee says the invoices were billed to it by mistake, were really expenses of a joint fundraising committee, and were rebilled there. Response.

Rep. Raja Krishnamoorthi (D-IL), Friends of Raja for Congress — RFAI on the April Quarterly Report asking for an explanation of apparent credits applied to debt owed to Spiros Consulting on Schedule D. Letter.

Sen. Katie Britt (R-AL), Britt for Alabama Inc — RFAI on the July Quarterly Report flagging contributions that appear excessive, prohibited or impermissible; the letter comes with a 24-page attachment. It lists, among others, Habib Debs (a $3,500 gift on 04/30/25 plus nine $500 monthly gifts, designated to the 2028 primary), Adena Friedman ($5,000 on 05/21/26) and two $2,500 gifts from Lincoln Financial Group PAC (05/06/25 and 06/30/26), plus long runs of small contributions from Peggy Jerome, Yvonne Lindecker, Robert Loughney, William McCann and Christine Ozburn. Letter.

Del. James Moylan (R-GU), James Moylan for Congress — three RFAIs, all about transfers from American Battleground Fund that look like joint-fundraising proceeds, though that committee is not listed as a joint fundraising representative on the Statement of Organization. The FEC asks the committee to amend the statement or the report and to add a memo Schedule A itemizing donors behind its share. Reports covered: July Quarterly 2026, April Quarterly 2026 and Year-End 2025.

Del. Kimberlyn King-Hinds (R-MP), King-Hinds for Congress — four RFAIs, the most of any committee in this batch. Three repeat the same American Battleground Fund joint-fundraising problem (Year-End 2025, October Quarterly 2025 and July Quarterly 2026). The July Quarterly 2026 letter also says memo entries on Schedule A understate cash on hand. A fourth, on the April Quarterly 2025 report, says the Column B year-to-date totals on lines 7(a), 7(c), 17 and 22 look wrong and the beginning cash balance does not match the 2024 Year-End ending balance. Letters: July Quarterly 2026, October Quarterly 2025, Year-End 2025, April Quarterly 2025.

sections.headline: 22 RFAIs from non-incumbent committees, two on unauthorized charges
paragraphs: Two letters (James Osyf for Congress, Friends of Chris Bennett) involve apparent unauthorized spending. Most others are routine: unremedied general-election contributions, missing 48-hour notices and amended-report explanations.

items: James Osyf for Congress (House candidate) — two RFAIs. The July Quarterly letter flags a $2,058.01 Schedule B disbursement labeled "Unauthorized transaction" as an apparent unauthorized disbursement of committee funds, noting the committee has already given an explanation. The April Quarterly letter says a $3,500.20 debt to Jones Mandel was dropped from the report. July letter · April letter.

Friends of Chris Bennett (House candidate) — RFAI on the amended April Quarterly Report about a $112.67 disbursement labeled "Unauthorized Charge, To Be Reimbursed." The FEC notes a reimbursement to Kari Shipman for "Reimbursement for Unauthorized Charges" and asks for more information as it becomes available. Letter.

Hoskins for IL 7 (House candidate) — two RFAIs. The April Quarterly letter cites apparent excessive contributions from Tom Needham ($2,500 on 08/03/25, $250 on 12/03/25, $1,000 on 03/11/26), general-election contributions that have not been refunded though the candidate is not in the general election, and a negative ending cash balance of $2,841.85. The July Quarterly letter flags a negative ending cash balance of $3,292.17. April letter · July letter.

Friends of Howard Rosenblum (House candidate) — April Quarterly RFAI. Five general-election contributions from June 2025 ($1,500 to $3,500 each, from Chris Estrin, Laura Gramer, Allan Rosenblum, Judith Rosenblum and Hermine Rothman) appear unremedied although the candidate will not be in the general election. It also lists a missing 48-hour notice for a $5,000 gift from the candidate on 03/02/26. Letter.

Elkind for New York (House candidate) — Year-End 2025 RFAI. The candidate is not seeking office, so six $3,500 general-election contributions (Bill Berkman, Nina Berkman, Ronit Berkman, Lisa Blatt, Jonathan Feigelson, Martin Peretz) must be refunded; refunds to Peretz and Blatt show on later reports but the FEC says the contributions still look unremedied. Letter.
Preston for Congress (House candidate) — April Quarterly RFAI on nine general-election contributions ($100 to $3,500, including $3,500 from Jon Walner) that appear unremedied. Letter.

Juliana for Illinois (Senate candidate) — April Quarterly RFAI on four missing 48-hour notices (Andrew McCollum $3,500; Kara Baysinger, Jennifer Byrd $1,000 each; Jennifer DiBrienza $3,500), and an unexplained $39,871.24 increase in vendor debts on the amended report. Letter.
Mark Nair for CD13 (House candidate) — amended April Quarterly RFAI on missing 48-hour notices for $1,938 from Texas Majority PAC and $5,000 from the candidate. Letter.

Michael Farrell for Utah (House candidate) — three RFAIs. The 12 Day Pre-Primary letter lists missing 48-hour notices for $50,000 from Michael Farrell and $1,000 from Susan Farrell (both 04/21/26) and earmarked contributions without conduit information. The amended Pre-Convention letter also cites missing conduit information. The July Quarterly letter says memo entries understate cash on hand. Pre-Primary · Pre-Convention · July Quarterly.

Driscoll for Congress (House candidate) — 12 Day Pre-Primary RFAI on $1,000 contributions on 05/26/26 from organizations not registered as political committees, including Citizens for Chris Schneider, East Rockaway Republican Finance Committee, Friends of John Giuffre, Friends of Kate Murray, Friends of Michael Giangregorio, Friends of Patrick Mullaney and Garden City Republican Club. It also asks for missing donor identification. Letter.

Melissa Bailey for Congress (House candidate) — two RFAIs (July Quarterly and amended April Quarterly) citing missing disbursement addresses (and purposes in the April report), payments to a "Credit Card Processing" conduit that implies earmarked contributions must be itemized, and unitemized candidate out-of-pocket spending. July letter · April letter.

Gregg Mele for America (House candidate) — amended Year-End 2025 RFAI saying loans to the committee noted as "Loan for Candidate Paid Expenses Itemized" look like advances and reimbursements misreported as loans, and asking about a $21,581.40 jump in both receipts and disbursements on the amendment. Letter.

Wilson for Congress (House candidate) — three RFAIs on amended reports, each asking why activity missing from the originals was not disclosed: $13,883.75 more in disbursements (amended 12 Day Pre-Primary), $51,433.42 more in receipts (amended July Quarterly 2026) and $42,146.54 more in disbursements (amended July Quarterly 2025). Pre-Primary · July 2026 · July 2025.
Dr. Sarah Sun Liew for U.S. Senate (Senate candidate) — July Quarterly RFAI saying the report was not on FEC Form 3 and must be resubmitted with filing software. Letter.

Western Alliance of Farmworker Advocates PAC — RFAI on an amended Statement of Organization: line 5(e) marks it a separate segregated fund, which requires a named connected organization (and the name must include it); otherwise the type of committee must be corrected. Letter.

sections.headline: Committees answer RFAIs; a former treasurer's restitution is the standout
paragraphs: Most are replies to September RFAIs. Forward Together PAC reports court-ordered restitution from its former treasurer; New Era Leadership admits a late independent-expenditure report.

items: Forward Together PAC — answers a September 1 RFAI on its July Quarterly Report. The committee reports a federal court ordered its former treasurer, Katherine Buchanan, to pay $29,413.77 in restitution, carried as a debt owed to the committee on Schedule D; it says it disclosed this on a July 20 Form 99 and continues to work with the FEC. Response.

New Era Leadership — admits a $25,000 supplemental advertising buy with AL Media LLC (part of a $150,000 buy) was disclosed 48 days late, on July 20, because a separate 24-hour independent-expenditure report was never filed by June 2. It says it has amended the reports, filed the late report, and notes the supported candidate lost. Response.

States Win — amended its July Quarterly: a 05/12/26 contribution from Vote Save America was reported as $5,000 but was $10,000 (refund pending), and a $5,000 transfer to its non-federal account, States Win, Inc., had been omitted. Response.
Mike Johnston for US Senate — replies to a September 2 RFAI about significant residual cash on hand, saying it is complying with restrictions and "weighing options" for the funds. Response.

Ola Victory Fund — says a $24,000 contribution of 12/31/25 from candidate Ola Nesheswat Hawatmeh's personal funds went through its link by mistake and was allocated entirely to People for Ola, so it was not excessive; it also asks to complete a pending termination review. Response.

Johnson Leadership Fund — says a contribution from Yum Brands Inc Good Government Fund (issued 02/12/26, deposited 05/07/26) was reported accurately and the event expenses were catering, site rental and travel. Response.
Campaign for Democracy PAC — says it already itemized every vendor payment behind travel and subsistence reimbursements over $500, so no amendment is needed. Response.

Massachusetts Republican Party and Los Angeles County Democratic Central Committee — each answers an RFAI about administrative expenses, saying salary and payroll costs were properly allocated because no employee spent more than 25% of their time on federal election activity. Massachusetts · Los Angeles County.
Lucio for Congress — Loan Forgiveness filing in which candidate Daniel Lucio forgives all remaining personal loans owed to him by the committee. Filing.
America Is the Way PAC — asks to terminate as a voluntary filer; registered September 3, 2026 and says it never received or spent money. Signed by treasurer Zachary J. Kuck. Filing.
Chuck Uribe for California Congressional District 4 — one-line statement that there was no activity. Filing.

You Can Push Back, Felicia Harris Hoss for Congress and Congressional Black Caucus PAC — Form 99 cover pages with no statement text in the PDF. You Can Push Back · Felicia Harris Hoss · Congressional Black Caucus PAC.
Aswar (House candidate) — a scanned paper FEC Form 3 report filed under the Form 99 type; the handwriting could not be reliably read. Filing.
